comparison: Both OpenEval and peer reviewers strongly support the temporal frequency tuning findings (C2, C3, C32-C46, C111-C115). OpenEval emphasizes the quantitative evidence and statistical rigor, while peer reviewers describe 'marked differences' and 'convincing evidence.' Both evaluations are aligned in finding this evidence compelling. Note that C35 appears in both, though OpenEval separately highlights it in R13.

Perfect agreement on orientation and direction selectivity findings (C4, C23-C31). Both evaluations support that early eye opening produces little or no difference in these properties. OpenEval notes the effects are 'small but statistically significant' for some comparisons, while peer reviewers accept this as part of the selective effects pattern.

Complete alignment on spatial frequency tuning preservation (C7, C47-C57). Both evaluations support that spatial frequency tuning remains largely intact despite premature visual experience. OpenEval emphasizes the comprehensive nature of measurements across multiple parameters, while peer reviewers accept this as demonstrating selective effects on temporal but not spatial processing.

Strong agreement on spontaneous activity increases (C5, C6, C68-C73). Both evaluations support the bilateral effects and global circuit change interpretation. OpenEval highlights the statistical robustness (p<0.0248 or better) and persistence of effects, while peer reviewers affirm the finding across all test configurations without challenge.

Both evaluations support the dissociation between unchanged peak responses and increased suppression (C58-C67). OpenEval emphasizes the particularly strong effect in EO1ipsi cells (p<1.59e-9), while peer reviewers note the changes in firing rate and suppression patterns. Both accept the findings as well-documented.

Divergence in evaluation type: OpenEval rates C74, C75, C8, C103 as UNCERTAIN, noting these are interpretations requiring behavioral testing to confirm the motion processing connection. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the interpretation and noting relevance to premature birth deficits. OpenEval is more cautious about inferential claims, while peer reviewers accept them as reasonable interpretations. Note that C104 is included in peer R6 but OpenEval addresses it separately in R16.

Divergence in evaluation type: OpenEval rates the evolutionary speculation (C9, C105) as UNCERTAIN, explicitly noting it is speculative and represents a hypothesis rather than demonstrated result. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting it as a reasonable conclusion. Both acknowledge the speculative nature, but differ on whether this warrants an UNCERTAIN vs SUPPORTED designation.

Perfect agreement on methodology (C16-C20, C106-C110). Both evaluations strongly support the experimental design and execution. OpenEval notes the methodology is 'sound for addressing the research questions,' while peer reviewers praise the 'carefully conducted study' and 'difficult to perform' experiments. Both accept without substantive critique.

Both evaluations support the background framework claims (C1, C10, C11, C21, C22), though peer R9 also includes C12-C15 which OpenEval addresses separately in R11 and R15. OpenEval emphasizes appropriate citations to established literature, while peer reviewers accept the developmental framework as established knowledge without challenge.

OpenEval separately highlights C35 (EO1ipsi temporal frequency effects) as noteworthy given cells viewed through naturally-opened eye, while peer reviewers include this claim within their broader evaluation of temporal frequency findings (R1) without special comment. Both support the finding but OpenEval gives it individual attention.

OpenEval addresses C104 (lasting effects summary) separately as SUPPORTED by collective experimental findings, while peer reviewers include it within their evaluation of clinical relevance and interpretation (R6). Both support the claim but group it differently in their evaluations.

OpenEval separately evaluates clinical literature background (C12, C13, C100-C102) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations, while peer reviewers include C12-C13 within their broader background framework evaluation (R9). Both accept these claims but OpenEval provides more granular analysis of the clinical context.

OpenEval separately evaluates ferret model rationale (C14, C15, C84) as SUPPORTED, while peer reviewers include C14-C15 within their broader background evaluation (R9). Both accept the ferret model as appropriate but OpenEval provides dedicated analysis of the model system justification.

OpenEval evaluates comparative literature claims (C76-C83) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate citations establishing novelty of temporal frequency deficits. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peer reviewers did not separately address these comparative literature claims.

OpenEval evaluates mechanistic background claims (C85-C96) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations for interpreting bilateral effects and circuit-level changes. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peer reviewers did not separately address these mechanistic background claims.

OpenEval evaluates cross-species comparison claims (C97-C99) as SUPPORTED, noting citations strengthening generalizability of premature sensory experience findings. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peer reviewers did not separately address these cross-species comparisons.
